headline: Malaysia Hosts 2.13 Million Registered Migrant Workers, Three Years at Tier 2 on Trafficking
context: The Human Resources Ministry told Parliament 2.13 million migrant workers held active registrations at 15 Oct 2025, down 13% in a year. The US TIP Report kept Malaysia at Tier 2 in 2025, citing no labour-trafficking prosecutions in palm oil or gloves, and in 2026.

changes.summary: Correction: Migrant worker count corrected from 2.1 million to about 2.5 million, and the TIP rating from Tier 2 Watch List to Tier 2. Removed unverified figures, including 68% with forced-labour indicators and RM48 billion of GDP.
Correction: Attributed the 2.5 million figure to MOF data and dated the Employment Act changes to 1 January 2023. Added MOF's top source countries: Bangladesh 37.8%, Indonesia 23.7%, Nepal 16.7%.

Correction: Malaysia had 2.13 million migrant workers with active registrations at 15 Oct 2025 (Dewan Rakyat, 3 Nov 2025); earlier editions said about 2.5 million, MOF's August 2024 figure. Malaysia was Tier 3 in 2021-2022 and the 2026 TIP Report kept it at Tier 2.

cards.big: Malaysia hosts 2.13 million registered migrant workers. The US TIP Report keeps flagging the same forced-labour patterns.
cards.sub: The 2026 TIP Report kept Malaysia at Tier 2. The 2025 report found no labour-trafficking prosecutions in palm oil or disposable-glove manufacturing.

cards.big: Since 1 September 2022 the Employment Act 1955 has covered anyone on a contract of service in Peninsular Malaysia, foreign workers included.
cards.sub: Indicators like passport confiscation, wage theft and debt bondage appear across sectors. The 2025 TIP says credible allegations went unaddressed.

cards.big: The US TIP Report's Tier 2 status reflects increasing efforts but unmet minimum standards in several key areas.
cards.sub: Convictions fell to 26 from 54 in the 2025 report, then rose to 36 in the 2026 report, which found no employment agency prosecuted for recruitment abuses.

cards.big: Foreign workers are officially allowed in manufacturing, construction, agriculture, plantations and services.
cards.sub: MOF end-August 2024: Bangladesh 37.8%, Indonesia 23.7% and Nepal 16.7% were the top source countries.

cards.big: Tier 2 is not a passing grade. Malaysia sat at Tier 3 in 2014 and again in 2021 and 2022, and still falls short of TVPA minimum standards.
Like a factory that treats its workers' welfare as a compliance line item: essential to hire, not to protect.
cards.sub: Documentation buys access to labour but not enforcement of the protections already in law.

cards.big: Wider Employment Act coverage is necessary but not sufficient. The 2025 TIP asks Malaysia to identify victims in palm oil and gloves and to prosecute trafficking cases.
